## Proof

Let \(B\) be the polar (associated symmetric bilinear) form of \(Q\), defined by
\[
B(x,y)=Q(x+y)-Q(x)-Q(y).
\]

**Step 1 — \(B\) is alternating in characteristic 2.**

For any \(x\in V\),
\[
B(x,x)=Q(2x)-2Q(x)=4Q(x)-2Q(x)=2Q(x)=0,
\]
since the field has characteristic \(2\). Hence \(B(x,x)=0\) for all \(x\), i.e. \(B\) is an *alternating* bilinear form.

**Step 2 — Non-degeneracy of \(Q\) forces \(B\) to be non-degenerate.**

By definition, a quadratic form \(Q\) is non-degenerate precisely when its polar form \(B\) is non-degenerate, i.e.
\[
\operatorname{rad}(B)=\{v\in V:B(v,w)=0\ \forall w\in V\}=\{0\}.
\]

**Step 3 — A non-degenerate alternating form exists only on an even-dimensional space.**

This is the standard structure theorem for alternating forms. Concretely: pick any nonzero \(v_{1}\in V\). Since \(B\) is non-degenerate, there exists \(w_{1}\in V\) with \(B(v_{1},w_{1})=1\). Then \(W_{1}=\operatorname{span}\{v_{1},w_{1}\}\) is a 2-dimensional non-degenerate subspace (a *hyperbolic plane*), and \(V=W_{1}\oplus W_{1}^{\perp}\) with \(W_{1}^{\perp}\) again non-degenerate alternating. Iterating,
\[
V \cong W_{1}\oplus W_{2}\oplus\cdots\oplus W_{k},
\]
an orthogonal direct sum of \(k\) hyperbolic planes. Therefore
\[
\dim V = 2k,
\]
which is even. (The iteration must terminate with the zero space, since a non-degenerate alternating space cannot be 1-dimensional: an alternating form on a 1-dimensional space is identically zero and hence degenerate.)

**Conclusion.** Combining Steps 1–3: the polar form of a non-degenerate quadratic form in characteristic \(2\) is a non-degenerate alternating bilinear form, which can exist only on an even-dimensional vector space. Hence

\[
\boxed{\dim V \text{ is even}.}
\]

### PROOF COMPLETE
